question: Do saved checkpoint-512 residual activations improve prediction of first natural close-thinking within the frozen 4096-token horizon beyond structural, current-readout confidence and fixed token-prefix features?

independent_verification.scope: Saved predictions/statistics and frozen provenance only; no refit or new inference

input_integrity: Exact saved prompt plus first512 generated IDs, no close cue or future tokens; every consumed payload size and SHA256 verified before parsing
activation_validation: CPU weights-only load, original serialized/content hashes, BF16 [28,2048], finite values; lossless float32 analysis copy

selection.grouping: Original problem identities; difficulty-stratified hash-ranked assignment before target derivation
selection.solver: L2 logistic regression, L-BFGS, max_iter10000, tol1e-6

baseline_definitions.A: Checkpoint geometry, problem token count, difficulty and train-vocabulary topic
baseline_definitions.B: A plus seven original current-readout confidence/agreement scalars; missingness preserved
baseline_definitions.Blex: B plus fixed unsigned hashed counts of trailing128 saved prefix tokens in512 buckets
baseline_definitions.Clex: Blex plus the same selected-layer residual vector
baseline_definitions.TRAIN_prevalence: Constant closure probability fitted by equal-problem TRAIN prevalence only

primary_paired_effect.comparison: Blex logloss minus Clex logloss on identical rows

secondary_paired_effect.comparison: B logloss minus C logloss at the same TRAIN-selected layer

uncertainty_scope: Problem-cluster intervals condition on the selected trained models; they omit training/model-selection uncertainty. Secondary and matched intervals are not multiplicity-adjusted and are not independent confirmation. PR-AUC, ROC-AUC and Brier are descriptive point estimates.
limitations: Retrospective endpoint pivot chosen after TRAIN measurement-failure aggregates; validation-heldout exploratory evaluation, not original confirmatory test.
Only32 heldout and17 matched problems; matched interval is wide and near zero at its lower limit.
Natural close-thinking is not mathematical correctness, solution quality, latent belief or answer recovery.
The fixed token-count baseline is not exhaustive observable semantics; activations are deterministic transformations of prefix/model input, not new information unavailable in the tokens.
Lexical augmentation did not improve B here; an activation gain is relative to these specified baselines, not every possible token-based model.
Features were reconstructed after terminal readouts; exact prefix-only information provenance is established, not physical pre-outcome recording.
No inference savings, safe early stopping, causal intervention or broad model/dataset generalization was tested.
